extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates reading Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions, and desired properties about quasiaffine morphisms, projective/regular models of curves, degree of finite maps of curves, and the desired axioms and basic theorems for Čech cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves (as presented in Vakil's text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiaffine scheme <=> OX ample (equivalence remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not hard to show that X is quasiaffine if and only if O_X is ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil notes the equivalence but says he won't use it here. This is a structural criterion: ampleness of the structure sheaf characterizes quasiaffineness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiaffine morphism (definition / equivalent condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is quasiaffine if the inverse image of every affine open subset of Y is a quasiaffine scheme. By Exercise 17.3.H this is equivalent to (under the stated hypotheses) Spec π_* O_X being … and the natural map X → Spec π_* O_X a quasicompact open embedding (π quasicompact and separated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use either the cover-by-affine-opens definition or the characterization via Spec of the pushforward of O_X; both are treated as equivalent in the text (modulo the cited exercise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change stability of quasiaffine morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Quasiaffine morphisms are preserved by base change: if X → Y is a quasicompact open embedding into an affine Y-scheme, then for any Y' → Y the base change X ×_Y Y' → Y' is a quasicompact open embedding into an affine Y'-scheme (hence quasiaffine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil emphasizes this property (and notes Exercise 17.3.H is not the right tool to show this fact). It shows quasiaffineness is stable under change of target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and local tests for quasiaffineness
rubrics_metrics.description: Quasiaffine morphisms are preserved by composition. Quasicompact locally closed embeddings are quasiaffine. If X is affine then a morphism X → Y is quasiaffine iff it is quasicompact. Any morphism from an affine scheme to a quasiseparated scheme is quasiaffine (from the Cancellation Theorem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are ways to recognize quasiaffine morphisms in practice: check composition, embeddings, or reduce to preimages of affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of regular projective model for integral curves (Theorem 17.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is an integral curve of finite type over a field k, then there exists a regular projective k-curve C' birational to C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil proves this by Noether normalization and taking normalization of P^1 in the function field; the statement is a core existence result used to compactify and regularize curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open embedding into projective regular curve for regular affine curves (Theorem 17.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is an irreducible regular curve, finite type over a field k, then there is an open embedding C ↪ C' into some projective regular curve C' over k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: embed affine C into A^n, consider closure in P^n, normalize the closure, and use Curve-to-Projective Extension arguments to extend from affine opens to the whole curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of several categories of curves (Theorem 17.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following categories are equivalent: (i) irreducible regular projective curves over k with surjective k-morphisms; (ii) same with dominant k-morphisms; (iii) same with dominant rational maps; (iv) integral curves of finite type over k with dominant rational maps; (v) opposite category of finitely generated fields of transcendence degree 1 over k with k-homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem identifies geometric objects (regular projective curves) with function-field data; the equivalences rely on compactification and normalization arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: π_* O_C locally free of finite rank for finite map to regular curve (Proposition 17.4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : C → C' is a surjective (dominant) map where C is a (pure dimension 1) curve with no embedded points and C' is a regular curve. Then π_* O_C is locally free of finite rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis 'no embedded points' means every associated point of C maps to a generic point of (some component of) C'. The proof reduces to checking constant rank at closed and generic points and reduces to discrete valuation ring local analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of degree of a finite morphism of curves (17.4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C' is irreducible, the rank of the locally free sheaf π_* O_C is the degree of π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the algebraic notion of degree for finite morphisms of curves; in the irreducible case it coincides with the degree of the extension of function fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree computations via scheme-theoretic fibers (Exercise 17.4.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p ∈ C' and the scheme-theoretic preimage π^*(p) has structure sheaf of dimension n as a k-vector space, then n = (deg π)(deg p). If C is regular and π^{-1}(p) = {p1,...,pm} and t is a uniformizer at p, then deg π = Σ_i val_{p_i}(π^* t) · deg(κ(p_i)/κ(p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formulas relate degree to lengths of fibers and to ramification multiplicities and residue field extensions; they connect algebraic degree to counting preimages with multiplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeros and poles count equality on irreducible regular curves (Exercise 17.4.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an irreducible regular curve C and a nonzero rational function s on C, the number of zeros of s (counted with multiplicity) equals the number of poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil suggests interpreting this as the degree of the morphism s : C → P^1; analytic readers can see it as a consequence of the Residue Theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber behavior and multiplicity types (revisiting Example 9.3.3 / 17.4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite map C → C' with rank d of π_* O_C, the fiber over any point (with residue field K) is Spec of an algebra of dimension d over K. There are three types of multiplicity behavior: split fibers over algebraic points (multiple distinct points), nonreduced fibers giving higher multiplicity at a single geometric point, and multiplicity arising from field extensions (residue-field extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil illustrates these with the example y^2 = x: fibers over x=1 (two distinct points), x=0 (one point with multiplicity 2 due to nonreducedness), x=-1 (one point over Q(i) giving multiplicity from field extension), and generic fiber behavior via function-field extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global reduction via discrete valuation rings (proof technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove constancy of rank of π_* O_C (hence local freeness), reduce the question to checking at the generic point and closed points by localizing at a maximal ideal to get a DVR and analyze module structure over that DVR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general method: reduce cohomological or finiteness statements to DVR/local analysis and rule out torsion summands using hypotheses (e.g., no embedded points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired properties/axioms of cohomology (overall list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vakil lists the key properties one wants from cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves on quasicompact separated A-schemes; these are enumerated (i)–(viii) and form the framework for further development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each property (i)–(viii) below is treated as a separate desideratum/criterion for any cohomology theory used in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality in sheaf: Hi is a covariant functor QCoh_X → Mod_A (property (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each i, Hi is a covariant functor from the category of quasicoherent sheaves on X to the category of A-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encodes naturality of cohomology with respect to maps of sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: H0 = global sections Γ (property (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor H0 is identified with Γ: H0(X, F) = Γ(X, F). Covariance for i=0 is the usual covariance of global sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This anchors higher cohomology as extensions of global sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in cohomology (property (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 of quasicoherent sheaves on X yields a long exact sequence ... → H^i(X,F) → H^i(X,G) → H^i(X,H) → H^{i+1}(X,F) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The connecting homomorphisms are part of the structure; this property is essential for many arguments (e.g., induction, vanishing results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality with respect to morphisms of schemes / Leray map (property (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a morphism of quasicompact separated A-schemes and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, there is a natural morphism H^i(Y, π_* F) → H^i(X, F) extending Γ; for G on Y one obtains pullback maps H^i(Y, G) → H^i(X, π^* G) via adjunction and covariance. This is part of the Leray spectral sequence picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These maps make Hi contravariant in the space and control how cohomology behaves under pushforward/pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine pushforward is cohomologically exact (property (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is an affine morphism and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, then the natural map H^i(Y, π_* F) → H^i(X, F) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular this lets one reduce cohomology computations for closed embeddings or affine morphisms to computations on the target (useful for calculations on projective schemes via PN_A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing beyond number of affines / dimensional vanishing (property (vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: If X can be covered by n affine open sets then H^i(X, F) = 0 for i ≥ n for all quasicoherent F. In particular, on affine schemes all higher (i>0) quasicoherent cohomology groups vanish. More generally if dim X = n then H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > n (dimensional vanishing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key vanishing principle used repeatedly (and leads to Serre's cohomological criterion for affineness when the vanishing holds for all i>0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre cohomological criterion for affineness (side remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact and quasiseparated and H^i(X,F)=0 for all i>0 and all quasicoherent F, then X is affine (in fact it suffices that H^1 of every quasicoherent ideal sheaf vanishes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil states this result (referring to GW) but does not prove it in the text at this point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation with direct sums / filtered colimits (property (vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Hi behaves well under direct sums and more generally under filtered colimits: Hi(X, lim_j F_j) = lim_j Hi(X, F_j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This controls cohomology on infinite constructions and is used in many limit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology of O(m) on P^n_A (Theorem 18.1.3 / property (viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: H^0(P^n_A, O(m)) is a free A-module of rank binomial(n+m, m) if m ≥ 0; H^n(P^n_A, O(m)) is a free A-module of rank binomial(-m-1, -n-m-1) (i.e., nonzero for m ≤ -n-1); and H^i(P^n_A, O(m)) = 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete computation is central: vanishing ranges, finite generation, top cohomology behavior and first appearance of Serre duality and Hilbert-polynomial phenomena are discussed here. (Vakil references Essential Exercise 14.1.C for H^0.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of cohomology on projective schemes (Theorem 18.1.4(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For any coherent sheaf F on a projective A-scheme X with A Noetherian, H^i(X, F) is a coherent (finitely generated) A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil proves this by resolution on projective space and downward induction using the computations for O(m). This is a key finiteness property (Grothendieck-style coherence theorem in projective case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre vanishing (Theorem 18.1.4(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a coherent sheaf F on a projective A-scheme X (even without Noetherian hypotheses in the stated form), for m ≫ 0 we have H^i(X, F(m)) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil proves this by twisting a surjection from sums of O(m) and inducting downward on cohomological degree; Serre vanishing is a fundamental tool for many projective arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-dimensionality of global sections for projective schemes (Corollary 18.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projective k-scheme has a finite-dimensional space of global sections H^0(X, O_X); more generally if A is Noetherian and F coherent on a projective A-scheme then H^0(X,F) is a coherent A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct corollary of the coherence theorem and Serre vanishing; Vakil emphasizes its surprising proof by descending induction on top cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward of coherent sheaves under projective morphisms is coherent (Exercise 18.1.B / coherence theorem remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a projective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, then the pushforward π_* of a coherent sheaf on X is a coherent sheaf on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil points to Grothendieck's Coherence Theorems for generalizations; this is used to deduce finiteness properties and characterize finiteness of morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective + affine characterization of finite morphisms (Corollary 18.1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose Y is locally Noetherian. Then π : X → Y is projective and affine if and only if π is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the coherence of π_* O_X to deduce finite type and finiteness; this gives a criterion to detect finiteness from projectivity+affineness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective + finite fibers = finite (Theorem 18.1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is projective with Y Noetherian, then π is finite iff it is projective and has finite fibers (equivalently projective and quasi-finite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil proves this by localizing on the target and choosing hypersurfaces to reduce to the projective+affine case; he notes a more general proper + finite fibers = finite holds under Noetherian hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Čech cohomology via a finite affine cover (18.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X quasicompact and separated, choose a finite affine open cover U = {U_i}. The Čech complex C^•(U, F) is formed from the sections on finite intersections and Hi_U(X,F) is the cohomology of this complex. For quasicoherent F the groups are A-modules (if X is an A-scheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil constructs the alternating-sum restriction maps explicitly and notes H^0_U(X,F) = Γ(X,F). Initially the groups depend on the cover; independence is proven next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of cover for Čech cohomology (Theorem 18.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X quasicompact and separated, Hi_U(X,F) is independent of the choice of finite affine cover U; the natural maps induced by refinements are isomorphisms, so define Hi(X,F) as the Čech cohomology groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to showing adding an extra open set doesn't change cohomology, using an exact sequence of complexes and vanishing of higher Čech groups on affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Čech cohomology vanishes on affines (Theorem 18.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is affine, then for any quasicoherent sheaf F and any finite affine cover U, the higher Čech cohomology Hi_U(X,F) = 0 for i > 0 (equivalently the augmented Čech complex with F(X) appended is exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vakil gives Serre's 'partition of unity' argument: reduce to the case where one cover element equals X and then localize to distinguished opens to reduce general covers to that case.
